clue.text: Supporting one of the Beatles in Melbourne's excellent

indicators.note: the drummer's name sits inside the Australian word, so 'in' signals a container

parts.note: beaut is Australian slang for excellent, hence the Melbourne flag
Ringo Starr was the Beatles' drummer

explanation.surface: A Beatle's Australian concert is praised as excellent by local fans.
explanation.walkthrough: BEAUT is Australian slang meaning excellent or great; 'Melbourne's' signals the Australian flavour.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear something out is to confirm or back it up, so the phrase means supporting a claim.

clue.text: Promote footballer

definitions.meaning: to ... a cause or candidate is to support and promote it
a full-... or defender in football is called a ...

explanation.surface: An instruction to push a football player's career forward.
explanation.definitionFit: Backing means championing, and a defensive football position is the back.

clue.text: Preacher has a job on the outskirts of Liege

parts.note: a post is a job or position

indicators.note: the outskirts of a word are its outer letters, the first and last

explanation.surface: A clergyman has found work in the suburbs of the Belgian city of Liège.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostles were the disciples sent out to preach the gospel, so one is a preacher.

clue.text: Drink from America co-eds brewed

indicators.note: brewing mixes ingredients together, so these letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: American college girls have mixed up a beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link word; the twelve letters of AMERICA CO-EDS rearrange into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This fizzy concoction of soda water with a scoop of ice cream is a sweet beverage.

clue.text: Receives help that's denied

parts.note: gains means receives or acquires
aid means help

explanation.surface: Someone is offered assistance that is then refused.
explanation.definitionFit: To gainsay is to contradict or deny, so its past tense means denied.

clue.text: A French port — open a bottle

parts.note: un is the French word for 'a'
Cork is a port city in southern Ireland

explanation.surface: In a French harbour town, someone pops open some wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulling out the stopper is how one opens a wine bottle.

clue.text: Southern racecourse excluding a northerner

indicators.note: excluding means the letter named is left out of the racecourse name

parts.note: Ascot is a famous racecourse in southern England, in Berkshire

explanation.surface: A racecourse in the south of England bans someone from the north.
explanation.walkthrough: ASCOT is the royal racecourse in Berkshire, southern England. 'Southern' could tempt you to take S; it is just part of the course's description.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Scotland comes from the north of Britain.

clue.text: Rough wind reported threatening ship

indicators.note: reported means the words are spoken, so we write what they sound like

parts.note: coarse means rough and air is a wind or breeze

explanation.surface: A storm at sea brings warnings of a menacing vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirate vessel from the Barbary coast was a menace to merchant shipping.

clue.text: Nottingham finally with place in Europe in draw showing Forest's limitations

indicators.note: the letters go inside the draw word, so 'in' signals a container

parts.note: a tie is a drawn match

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of Nottingham

parts.note: Berlin is the German capital

explanation.surface: Nottingham Forest draw a match in Europe, exposing the football club's weaknesses.
explanation.walkthrough: Nottingham Forest is an English football club; here 'Forest' means trees.
explanation.definitionFit: The altitude above which trees cannot grow marks the edge of woodland, its limit on a mountainside.

clue.text: Knot that requires cold attachment — snag!

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
an attachment to someone is affection or love
a hitch is a snag or problem

explanation.surface: Tying a knot needs a chilly fitting, and there's a problem.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a sailor's tie made of two turns round a post, a standard type of knot.

clue.text: Tot sees doctor before noon

parts.note: a.m. means before midday

explanation.surface: A small child visits the GP in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: A tot is a small measure of spirits such as whisky.

clue.text: Dish in kitchen where they're all hoping for a strike

definitions.text: where they're all hoping for a strike

parts.note: a bowl is a dish
taken as written
a galley is a ship's or aircraft's kitchen

explanation.surface: A dish sits in a kitchen where the workers all want to walk out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike' looks like industrial action; in tenpin bowling it means knocking all the pins down with one ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenpin players at this venue each want to topple every pin with a single ball.

clue.text: Mix porridge

definitions.meaning: porridge is British slang for a prison sentence

explanation.surface: A recipe instruction to blend the oats.
explanation.walkthrough: Porridge, besides oats, is British slang for time in prison; stir is slang for prison too.
explanation.definitionFit: Stirring blends ingredients, and both words are slang for jail time.

clue.text: Replacement of trouser damaged round top of groin area

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round the others, so 'round' signals a container
damaged means the letters are knocked out of shape and rearranged
top of picks the first letter of groin

explanation.surface: Someone needs new trousers after ripping them around the crotch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' turns TROUSER into SURROTE, which goes 'round' G and A.
explanation.definitionFit: A surrogate is a substitute standing in for another person.

clue.text: Make smooth run in heritage railway?

indicators.note: the letter goes inside the railway, so 'in' signals a container

parts.note: a heritage railway runs old steam trains, so a steam line
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A train trip on a preserved line could be made more efficient.
explanation.walkthrough: Heritage railways are preserved lines running vintage steam trains.
explanation.definitionFit: To streamline is to make a shape smoother, or a process simpler.

clue.text: Relating to a subject — one that's generally taught seeing ma's not around

indicators.note: the letters of ma's are missing from the outside of the subject, its start and end

parts.note: maths is a subject taught in nearly every school
the letters MA and S, taken as written

explanation.surface: A lesson on a topic goes on while mother is away.
explanation.walkthrough: MA comes off the front and S off the back, the 'around' of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something concerned with a theme or topic is described this way.

clue.text: Blooming female learner seen before test

parts.note: L is for learner, as on L-plates
an oral is a spoken exam

explanation.surface: A young woman learning to drive faces her driving test.
explanation.definitionFit: Something full of flowers, like a print or arrangement, is in bloom.

clue.text: Tradition supported by the Queen as patron

indicators.note: in a down entry, the queen goes underneath the tradition, holding it up

parts.note: a custom is a tradition
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A tradition has royal patronage.
explanation.definitionFit: A patron of a shop or business is a regular client.

clue.text: Cut tax

definitions.meaning: ... duty is a tax on goods

explanation.surface: A demand to lower duties.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for removing by cutting and a noun for a duty on goods.

clue.text: Dog, right one to work in pit

parts.note: a collie is a sheepdog

explanation.surface: A dog and a man are sent down to dig.
explanation.definitionFit: A collier is a coal miner, a worker underground in a mine.

clue.text: New York guy's after kicks in Morecambe, say

indicators.note: after tells us the New York guy comes behind the kicks

parts.note: kicks are thrills or fun
a guy is a man; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: An American gets his thrills at a seaside town in Lancashire.
explanation.walkthrough: Morecambe is a Lancashire resort, but Eric Morecambe was a much-loved British comedian.
explanation.definitionFit: Eric Morecambe was a comedian, an example of a professional comic.

clue.text: One's shaken, not stirred, seeing skill in car

indicators.note: the skill sits inside the car, so 'in' signals a container

parts.note: the Mini is a small British car
art means skill

explanation.surface: James Bond's drink order alongside a skilful drive.
explanation.walkthrough: James Bond orders his vodka martini 'shaken, not stirred'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bond's favourite cocktail is famously served shaken rather than stirred.

clue.text: Book space

explanation.definitionFit: A tome is one book, and the measure of three-dimensional space is its capacity.

clue.text: Clumsy admiral to set out

indicators.note: set out means laid out in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An awkward naval commander is about to embark.
explanation.definitionFit: Maladroit is a French-derived word for awkward or inept.

clue.text: A jumper's shrunk — will it go over one's head?

definitions.text: will it go over one's head?

indicators.note: shrunk means the animal's name loses its last letter

parts.note: a frog is a jumper; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A sweater has shrunk in the wash, so will it still fit over your head?
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' suggests a sweater, as in British English; here it is a frog.
explanation.definitionFit: This rounded hairstyle sits on top of the head.

clue.text: The sound of a horse that's eaten nothing, waiting impatiently

indicators.note: the horse eats the zero, so it takes the letter inside

parts.note: a gee-gee is a horse, and GG is how it sounds spelt as letters
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A hungry horse that has had no food waits eagerly.
explanation.walkthrough: Gee-gee is childish British for a horse; said aloud as letters it is GG, so 'a horse' becomes A GG.
explanation.definitionFit: Agog means eagerly expectant, keen to know what happens.

clue.text: Bird nesting in hibiscus

indicators.note: nesting in means the bird sits hidden among the letters of the flowering shrub

explanation.surface: A bird makes its nest in a flowering shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibis is a long-billed wading bird.

clue.text: Striking assorted elements of plum mingle

indicators.note: assorted means the parts of these words are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Fruit ingredients are being blended together.
explanation.definitionFit: Pummelling is beating with repeated blows, which is striking.

clue.text: Peer ahead endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly means the word for ahead loses its final letter

parts.note: early means ahead of time

explanation.surface: An instruction to look forward continually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peer' looks like a verb meaning to look; it is the noun for a nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: An earl is a member of the nobility, a peer of the realm.

clue.text: Cockney who's decorated a line in old capital

indicators.note: these letters go inside the old capital, so 'in' signals a container

parts.note: Peking is the old Western name for Beijing, China's capital
RLY is the abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: A Londoner received an honour while on a railway trip in old China.
explanation.walkthrough: Pearly kings and queens are London East End charity figures whose clothes are covered in mother-of-pearl buttons.
explanation.definitionFit: These East End figures wear suits sewn all over with pearl buttons, so they are decorated Londoners.
